title: Find the Number of Subarrays Where Boundary Elements Are Maximum
summary: Given an array of positive integers, count the subarrays where the first and last elements are the maximum value within the subarray.
statement: Given an array of positive integers, count the subarrays where the first and last elements are the maximum value within the subarray.
constraints: Count nonempty contiguous subarrays whose first and last values are equal to the maximum value appearing anywhere inside that subarray.
hints: For a right boundary value x, valid left boundaries are earlier equal x values with no intervening value greater than x.
Maintain a decreasing stack of values and counts since the most recent larger blocker.
Pop smaller values; push x with count one or increment its equal top count; add that count to the answer.
After popping, the equal top entries are exactly the valid left boundaries ending here, including the current singleton.
editorial: After popping, the equal top entries are exactly the valid left boundaries ending here, including the current singleton.

tests.explanation: All five singletons qualify, and subarray [3,3] adds one, for six total.
Four singletons plus [3,1,3], the final [3,3], and the whole array give seven.
